key_insight: Matching pin and shoulder eccentricities synchronizes tool runout, stabilizing material flow and preventing defects observed with pin eccentricity alone.
engineering_relevance: Coordinating pin and shoulder offsets offers a potential route to defect-free friction stir welds despite unavoidable industrial tool runout.
method: Experimentally compare pin-only eccentricity with equal pin and shoulder offsets.
Evaluate weld defects and microstructural evolution under each eccentricity condition.
Interpret deformation and thermal histories using the Zener–Hollomon parameter.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports wormholes and surface grooves with increasing pin-only eccentricity, but sound welds with matched offsets, alongside differences in recrystallization, grain refinement, and precipitation behavior.
watch_item: The abstract provides no eccentricity ranges, quantitative defect metrics, or operating limits, so applicability beyond the tested conditions remains uncertain.
paper_title: Mechanistic Insights into Coupled Pin Shoulder Eccentricity for Controlling Defect Formation and Microstructural Evolution in Friction Stir Welding
